  This is the time set aside for members of the public to address the City Council on
  items of interest that are not on the Agenda, but are within the subject matter

  In an effort to provide everyone with an opportunity to speak tonight, please be

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  This is the presentation of the “Register of Demands and Warrants” for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of February 19, 2019.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of February 19, 2019.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. RESOLUTION NO. 19-06 – RESOLUTION FOR A LONG-TERM TEMPORARY
  STREET CLOSURE ON PADILLA STREET

  The owner/applicant, Global Eagle Medical Center LLC, of the project located
  at 508 West Las Tunas Drive is requesting a long-term temporary closure for
  construction staging purposes and to have access onto the property due to site
  restrictions. This closure on Padilla Street will take place from Santa Anita Street
  to 250 feet west of Santa Anita Street. The timeframe of the closure is March
  2019 to June 2021. Pedestrian access to Padilla Street west of Santa Anita will
  be provided at all times via the existing public sidewalk on the south side of
  Padilla Street.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-06,
  authorizing the long-term temporary street closure of Padilla Street from Santa
  Anita Street to 250 feet west of Santa Anita Street.

  D. PURCHASE OF GRANT FUNDED MOBILE DATA NETWORK EQUIPMENT
  AND MOBILE DATA COMPUTERS

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 5, 2019  3
   As a member of Verdugo Fire Communications, the San Gabriel Fire
  Department is required to maintain radio and mobile data system equipment
  that meets Verdugo operating requirements. The Computer Aided Dispatch
  used by Verdugo is undergoing a major upgrade after nearly 30 years in service.
  The enhanced system structure requires Verdugo users to replace data
  connectivity capabilities in all field apparatus. $60,000.00 in State Homeland
  Security Grant Program (SHSGP) 2017 Grant funding covering 100% of the
  purchase price of the required equipment and installation has been identified
  and approved for this project.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Authorize an increase to the Estimated Revenue Budget Account #186-
  3215;
  2. Motion pursuant to San Gabriel Municipal Code 34.31(E) to waive the
  bidding procedures of 34.31(E) based on a finding of the need to sole source
  the purchase (MDC) and piggybacking onto the Glendale RFP (Modems, et
  al); and
  3. Motion to approve purchase Cradlepoint Broadband Modems, Routers,
  Antennas, Cables from Presidio and five (5) Radio Mobile Patriot MDC’s
  from Radio Mobile, Incorporated for the amount of $60,028.68 with 2017
  SHSGP funds in the amount of $60,000 charged to account #122-761-57-
  99-380 and $28.68 charged to account #121-761-00-21-000.

  E. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 19-08, AUTHORIZING DESIGNATED CITY
  OFFICIALS TO OPEN, MAINTAIN AND MAKE TRANSACTIONS IN CITY
  ACCOUNTS IN VARIOUS BANKS AND FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS

  The City maintains accounts with various banking institutions in accordance
  with the City’s Investment Policy and State Law. With the retirement of the
  former Finance Director, it is necessary to update the signature authority to
  remove the former Finance Director and add our Interim Finance Director.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-08,
  authorizing designated City officials to open, maintain and make transactions
  in City accounts in various banks and financial institutions.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 5, 2019  4
   F. REQUEST FOR UNALLOCATED COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK
  GRANT FUNDS TO PURCHASE EQUIPMENT FOR THE COMMUNITY
  SERVICES YOUTH PROGRAM

  The City of San Gabriel receives Community Development Block Grant (CDBG)
  funds for the Community Services Youth Program. Through the Los Angeles
  County Community Development Commission, CDBG funds assist in operating
  youth programs at McKinley Elementary School, Vincent Lugo Park and Smith
  Park for low and moderate income participants.

  During the past year, the City has had just under $130,000 in unallocated CDBG
  funds. The County has encouraged the City to utilize the unallocated funds. The
  Community Services Department is requesting City Council approval to
  increase the CDBG Youth Program budget $2,500 from the unallocated funds.
  These funds will assist in purchasing equipment for the All-City Pentathlon and
  the youth summer programs.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve an increased estimated
  revenue of $2,500 to account #185-3218 and an increased budget
  appropriation of $2,500 to Community Services Youth Program account #185-
  850-20-21-000.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. PUBLIC HEARING TO ESTABLISH THE SAN GABRIEL TOURISM AND
  MARKETING IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT

  The San Gabriel Tourism and Marketing Improvement District (SGTMID) is a
  benefit assessment district proposed to create a revenue source to help fund
  marketing and sales promotion efforts for San Gabriel lodging businesses and
  thereby increase the transient occupancy tax for the City of San Gabriel. This
  approach has been used successfully in other destination areas throughout the
  state to improve tourism and drive additional room night sales to assessed
  lodging businesses. The proposed SGTMID includes all lodging businesses, with
  100 rooms or more, located within the boundaries of the City of San Gabriel.

  San Gabriel lodging business owners with 100 rooms or more decided to
  pursue formation of the SGTMID in order to create a revenue source devoted
  to marketing San Gabriel as a tourist, meeting and event destination. If
  established, the SGTMID would generate approximately $193,000 on an annual
  basis for promotion of travel and tourism specific to San Gabriel.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 5, 2019  5
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council hold a public hearing, declare results of
  majority protest proceedings, and adopt Resolution No. 19-09, resulting in the
  establishment of the San Gabriel Tourism and Marketing Improvement District
  pursuant to the Property and Business Improvement District Law of 1994.
